reviews.title: Don’t use if you’re not 100% confident in what you’re doing
reviews.text: The entire process for setting up the Google authenticator is not intuitive and the instructions are not easily accessible. Plus, it doesn’t warn you that when you set up this kind of two factor authentication that you will no longer be able to access your account in other ways that you were used to. Especially if you don’t have a second device. There are many people with only one device out there and for those of you who do not have a second device, you will be locked out of your account if you set this up. This little fact should be included on the pages where one makes the decision to start to factor authentication because it’s not listed anywhere and it’s really hard to get out of once you make that mistake.

reviews.title: No real way to recover my own Google account while abroad
reviews.text:
I am extremely frustrated with Google account recovery.

I created this account myself. I know the email address. I know the password. But Google still blocks me from signing in because I am currently in another country and cannot confirm the login from an old device that is physically unavailable.

The main problem is this: Google does not even give me meaningful recovery questions to answer. I am simply told that I did not provide enough information, while no real alternative path is offered.

This creates an absurd situation:
- I know the login credentials
- I am the legitimate account owner
- I am willing to verify ownership
- but Google gives me no practical way to do so

Telling users to use the old device or familiar Wi-Fi is not a real solution when that device is unavailable or located in another country. People travel, move, lose devices, replace devices, and still need access to their own accounts.

My complaint is not only about access to this account, but also about the lack of a real escalation path. There is no clear way to contact an actual support agent, no meaningful appeal process, and no transparent explanation of what exact proof would be sufficient.

Please explain:
1. What exact recovery options exist when the old device is unavailable
2. Why password knowledge is treated as insufficient with no alternative verification path
3. How a legitimate user located abroad is supposed to recover access
4. Where a user can submit a formal complaint and receive an

I have a lot of accounts on the app so the search feature is very helpful. However if you need to edit or remove an account you are not able to do this from the search results view, so I have to scroll through many many accounts to find and edit the account I am looking for. 

Also the display listing emphasises the code numbers rather than the name of the account making it harder to see/find the name of the account you want a code for. 

Authy and Microsoft Authenticator do it much better. 

I hope this app will be improved.

reviews.title: Google will not help you!
reviews.text: I cannot stress this enough. This app works really well and it’s a good way to keep all your accounts safe.  These keys will not upload to your Google account to transfer between new devices like if you get a new phone. Unless you check the cloud update Box. If you lose the old device without transferring all of your new stuff from the Authenticator onto the new device before getting rid of it you are practically screwed and have to start all over again. So if you use this, make quadruplet sure. You have every back up in place if you lose the authenticator access on your phone. I would also like to add that Google will not help you. They do not have a health center anymore that has real people that work for Google helping you. They will leave you high and dry. Just keep in mind before using.
